after.problem: An arithmetic series has the first term ${a}_{1}=5$, the second term is ${a}_{2}=15$, and the sum of the series is ${S}_{N}=845.$ Find the number of terms $N$ in the series.
after.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series.

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d)
$$

Since we know the first two terms of the arithmetic series, we can find its common difference, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =15-5 \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting ${a}_{1}=5$, $d=10$, and ${S}_{N}=845$ into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ 845 & =\frac{N}{2}(2(5)+(N-1)(10)) \\ 845 & =\frac{N}{2}(10+10N-10) \\ 845 & =\frac{N}{2}(10N) \\ 845 & =5{N}^{2} \\ 169 & ={N}^{2} \\ N & =13\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we take the positive square root because $N$ can't be negative.

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =3-1 \\  & =2\end{aligned}

$$

$$

after.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series:

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d)\,\,
$$

We have been given the sum ${S}_{N}=180$, and the first term ${a}_{1}=5.$ Our goal is to find $N,$ the number of terms.

The common difference $d$ can be found, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =15-5 \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ 180 & =\frac{N}{2}(2\cdot 5+(N-1)\cdot 10) \\ 180 & =\frac{N}{2}(10+10N-10) \\ 180 & =\frac{N}{2}(10N) \\ 180 & =5{N}^{2} \\ 36 & ={N}^{2} \\ N & =6\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: An arithmetic series has the $6$th term ${a}_{6}=17,$ the $9$th term ${a}_{9}=26,$ and the sum of the series is ${S}_{N}=77.$ Find the number of terms $N$ in the series.
after.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series.

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d)
$$

Since we know two terms of the arithmetic series, we can find its common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\frac{{a}_{9}-{a}_{6}}{9-6} \\  & =\frac{26-17}{9-6} \\  & =\frac{9}{3} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

We know that ${a}_{6}=17.$ We can compute ${a}_{1}$ using the formula for the $n$th term, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\ 17 & ={a}_{1}+(6-1)\cdot 3 \\ 17 & ={a}_{1}+15 \\ {a}_{1} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting ${a}_{1}=2,$ $d=3,$ and ${S}_{N}=77$ into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ 77 & =\frac{N}{2}(2\cdot 2+(N-1)\cdot 3) \\ 154 & =N(4+3N-3) \\ 154 & =N(3N+1) \\ 154 & =3{N}^{2}+N \\ 3{N}^{2}+N-154 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

For the equation above, the quadratic formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}N & =\frac{-1\pm \sqrt{(1)^{2}-4\cdot 3\cdot (-154)}}{2\cdot 3} \\  & =\frac{-1\pm \sqrt{1\,849}}{6} \\  & =\frac{-1\pm 43}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $N=7$ or $N=-\frac{22}{3}.$ We disregard the negative solution since $N$ must be positive.

Therefore, our series has $N=7$ terms.
